claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl coating deposited from 15–45 μm feedstock falls short of the required thickness.
Changing the feedstock distribution from 15–45 μm to approximately 30–75 μm will increase coating thickness.
The coarser feedstock will preserve coating integrity.
The coarser feedstock will keep as-sprayed oxidation minimal.
Larger particles produce thicker molten splats on impact.
Larger particles have greater mass and a lower surface-to-volume ratio than finer particles.
A lower particle surface-to-volume ratio reduces relative in-flight oxidation.
Increasing particle size improves deposition efficiency.
Greater mass deposited per splat produces a thicker overall coating.
The 30–75 μm feedstock will produce a cohesive coating with microstructural integrity similar to that produced from finer powder.
The thicker coating will retain the desired phase structure.
The thicker coating will retain baseline adhesion properties.
Excessively large particles can remain incompletely melted or generate adverse defects.
Controlling spray energy and the deposition environment can prevent excessive oxidation.
The intervention will remain effective during high-temperature cycling typical of aero-engine thermal-barrier-coating service.
A thickness increase below 10%, or oxidation that compromises mechanical integrity relative to the baseline, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies changing particle size while keeping every other processing parameter constant, but the uncertainty statement says successful performance may depend on fine-tuning spray parameters alongside the new feedstock.
